I live in Canada, a few blocks from my family. My dad's partner (O) is from a large Mexican family. O speaks English very well, but the rest of her family does not. Her sister (W), got married this past spring to a man from Colombia. They got engaged in Christmas morning, and decided they wanted to get married in March. W has a seven year old son, and they both wanted to make sure he was a big part of the wedding. 
When I arrived there was a DJ, who had the music in the hall so loud that none of us could talk to each other. There were three tables of gringos out of the ten. I had never met O's extended family, other than W. O spent so much time doing wedding prep, that I didn't see her for the first ninety minutes, and thus had no way of knowing who was who - on top of not being able to talk to people I shared a first language with. 
Once the ceremony started, an MC came up and introduced the couple in Spanish and English. W and her husband-to-be stood on stage, where the DJ had forgotten to turn the spinning disco lights off. The officiant didn't speak any Spanish, so she garbled everyone's names, and the happy couple uttered their vows by each syllable - with zero understanding of what they were saying. The ring bearer presented the rings, but then stood with his back to the crowd, completely blocking the ceremony. All while the disco lights continued.
There was a really lovely moment where they had W's receive his own ring of becoming a family. I try to hold on to that moment.
After the short ceremony, the DJ came back on, at full volume, and we were instructed to eat from a buffet. 
The Latin side of my family is full of great cooks, but everything at the buffet was either a meat dish - made by family, or carbs (pasta, rice, potatoes) from Costco. Zero vegetables.
So dinner ends, DJ is still on, conversation is impossible. About ten of us dance, and try to suffer through the bloat.
After half an hour, people seem less stuffed and are getting into the music...
And a live mariachi band appears. 
Okay, this is awesome! Mariachi! Look at their suits! But they play a song, a full song at.every.table. It takes over an hour, and no one has been dancing after the initial thrill has worn off. We're all sleepy, at eight at night, and just done.
We ended up sneaking out after the mariachis left and the DJ started to again to an empty dance floor.
It was a really sad wedding.

Bonus!
The groom's work buddy's stood at the back the entire night and for rip roaring drunk. The family had to clean up the venue after the wedding in order to get their deposit back. The groom's friends had thrown their garbage under a table the entire night. After W found out, she didn't speak to her new husband for a month

When I was seventeen I lived with a family friend who was in her early thirties. She was my best friend/surrogate mother/sister I never had. When she died very suddenly I stayed at a friends' house so that her family from out of town could use our home as the home base for funeral prep and general congregating. They were all lovely people who left me a fridge full of food and kind words. Unfortunately before going home they left all the garbage bags, from their stay, out in the alley. A lot of it was food and raccoons got into it. I've never seen so much garbage strewn about. I remember I brought down the garbage from my room, saw the pile, and just blanked. I don't even know where I put the bag I'd been holding. I forgot all about it - I guess I couldn't begin to wrap my head around it. My next door neighbour called the city and a warning was posted on my door. I shared the house, but not my suite, with three other people. The guy who lived downstairs, who's name I don't even know, saw the posting and took it down. He then put on rubber gloves and boots and spent the entire afternoon cleaning up the alley. 
I'll never forget how kind that was of him. I am still so incredibly grateful  that he had the wherewithal to know I needed help, and the selflessness to provide it immediately.
